chunks.text:
What is Datawrap?
Datawrap is a universal data transfer platform. Transfer Studio maps schemas across systems, runs nine preflight gates before any production write, and proves every load with checksum reconciliation. Datawrap Pilot and MCP bring the same governed engine to chat and agent workflows.

Product surfaces (sidebar map)
The signed-in workspace sidebar matches these guides. Start in Transfer Studio, then expand to Pipelines, Contracts, Pilot, and MCP.
Platform — Overview, Transfer Studio, Connectors, Contracts
Operations — Jobs (Job Theater), Pipelines, Transforms, Query, Pilot
System — Settings (SSO/Team), MCP, Help, Proofs
Governed path — Source → Destination → Map → Validate → Run → Jobs proof
Overview — full Platform / Operations / System sidebar used across every guide.

Your first transfer (step by step)
Follow this exact path inside the signed-in workspace. Every screenshot is from the live application — not a marketing mock.
Confirm the workspace is healthy
Open **Overview** and confirm connection health, recent jobs, and throughput for your tenant. If metrics fail to load, fix connectivity with your Owner before creating connectors.

You should see live **rows moved**, success rate, and connection status cards before you continue.
Where: Sidebar → Overview
Add or test a connector
Open **Platform → Connectors**. Click **New connection** to create a source or destination, or click **Test** on an existing row until you see **Test passed**.

For a quick offline walkthrough you can skip connectors and upload a CSV on the Transfer Studio **Source** step instead.
Where: Platform → Connectors → New connection
Run Transfer Studio Source → Destination → Map → Validate → Run
Open **Platform → Transfer** (or **New transfer**). On **Source**, upload a sample file such as `sample-orders.csv` or pick a **Database** connector. Review **Detected structure**, then continue through **Destination**, **Map**, and **Validate**.

Fix every blocked gate before **Run**. Execute stays locked until Validate passes.
Where: Platform → Transfer  ·  or New transfer
Prove the load in Job Theater
Open **Operations → Jobs** and select the run. Confirm **Quarantine** is empty (or review each rejected value and reason). Wait for checksum **MATCH** and row fidelity on the reconcile stage — that is the archiveable proof of the load.
Where: Operations → Jobs

Workspace concepts
Every transfer runs inside a workspace with connectors, saved routes, synonym dictionaries, and audit history. Team members inherit RBAC from your IdP in enterprise tenants.
Connectors — encrypted credentials scoped to workspace
Saved routes — reuse mapping + write mode presets
Synonym dictionary — accepted semantic pairs for auto-map
Job Theater — unified run history with quarantine and proof

What your organization receives
Datawrap is delivered as a **hosted enterprise workspace** at your tenant URL (for example `your-company.datawrap.io`). After sign-in you work entirely in the browser — there is nothing to install on operator laptops.

The signed-in product includes **Overview**, **Connectors**, **Transfer Studio**, **Pipelines**, **Jobs** (Job Theater), **Query**, **Pilot**, and **Settings**. Your IT team configures SSO and optional BYOK once; day-to-day operators create connections, run governed transfers, and prove loads.
After SSO — Overview shows workspace health, throughput, and recent jobs for your tenant.

Procedure: get access
Use this path when onboarding a new operator or confirming a newly provisioned tenant. Complete every step before you create production connectors.
Receive your tenant URL and role
A workspace **Owner** (or Datawrap provisioning) invites you by email with one of three roles:

**Viewer** — inspect Jobs, quarantine, and MATCH proof; cannot create connectors or run transfers.

**Editor** — create connectors, run **Transfer Studio** and **Pipelines**, and open **Job Theater**.

**Owner** — everything Editors can do, plus **Settings → SSO**, **Enterprise**, **BYOK**, **Team**, and API keys.

Open the invite link, or go directly to your tenant URL (for example `https://your-company.datawrap.io`). Sign in with your company identity provider — **Okta**, **Azure AD / Entra ID**, **Google Workspace**, or another SAML 2.0 / OIDC IdP configured for the tenant.
Where: IT / Datawrap admin → invite email
Sign in with SSO
On the login screen choose **Continue with SSO** (or your company's branded SSO button). Authenticate with your work account. Datawrap issues a workspace session that inherits your RBAC role from the invite or from IdP group claims.

A successful sign-in lands on **Overview**. Confirm the top bar shows your tenant name and that the left sidebar lists **Platform** surfaces (Connectors, Transfer, Pipelines) and **Operations → Jobs**. If you only see a blank or permission error, stop and ask an Owner to verify your role under **Settings → Team**.
Where: Login → Continue with SSO
Confirm you can reach Connectors and Transfer
In the left sidebar open **Platform → Connectors**. You should see health cards and either an empty Connections table or existing rows. Then open **Platform → Transfer** (Transfer Studio) or click **New transfer** if shown.

You are ready for day-one work when:

**1.** **New connection** is visible on Connectors (Editors and Owners).

**2.** Transfer Studio opens the **Source → Destination → Map → Validate → Run** wizard.

**3.** **Operations → Jobs** opens Job Theater for past and live runs.

If Connectors or Transfer is missing from the sidebar, your role is likely **Viewer** — ask an Owner to raise it to **Editor** under **Settings → Team**.
Where: Sidebar → Platform → Connectors  ·  Transfer
Tip: **Viewer** — inspect Jobs and proof only. **Editor** — run transfers and manage connectors. **Owner** — SSO, BYOK, Team invites, and enterprise controls under **Settings**.

Admin checklist (Owners)
Tenant **Owners** complete these once per workspace. Operators do not need this checklist to run day-to-day transfers — it is for IT and security readiness.
**Settings → SSO** — choose SAML or OIDC, paste IdP metadata URL (or upload XML), map roles if your IdP sends group claims, then click **Test login** and **Save**.
**Settings → Enterprise** — set tenant display name, data **region**, MFA policy, session timeout, and optional IP allowlist.
**Settings → Enterprise → BYOK** — upload your customer KMS key when procurement requires customer-managed encryption for connector secrets.
**Settings → Team** — invite Editors and Viewers with least privilege; re-check IdP group → role mapping after SSO enforce.
**Settings → Security** — download the **Security posture report** for SOC 2 / GDPR / HIPAA questionnaires.
Tip: If your tenant URL is not live yet, email **sales@datawrap.io**. Provisioning is handled by Datawrap — operators never install or run a local API.

Supported browsers & network
Use a current **Chromium**, **Firefox**, or **Safari** build. Connector **Test** and transfers need outbound network access from the Datawrap worker (in your pinned region) to your sources and destinations — databases, warehouses, and object stores.

Corporate proxies and firewalls must allow those destinations for the workspace region selected under **Settings → Enterprise**. If **Test** fails with a timeout while credentials are correct, open a ticket with network/security before re-running Validate gates in Transfer Studio.

chunks.section_title: Example transfer used in this guide
chunks.text:
Example transfer used in this guide
Every screenshot below is from a real Transfer Studio session using the built-in demo file.

**Source:** `sample-orders.csv` (5 rows · 5 columns: `order_id`, `customer_email`, `order_amt`, `order_date`, `status`)

**Destination:** **File Export** → **CSV** → `exports/sample-orders.csv`

**Path:** **Source → Destination → Map → Validate → Run** — the same rail Pipelines, Pilot, and MCP reuse. There is no silent shortcut around gates or checksum proof.

For production warehouse loads, swap Destination to **Database / Warehouse** and pick a saved connector (for example PostgreSQL `public.orders`). Map, Validate, and Run stay identical.

Procedure: run the sample-orders transfer
Follow all five steps in order. Markers on each screenshot match the live product UI.
Step 1 — Source: load sample-orders.csv
Open **Transfer Studio** from the sidebar (**Transfer**) or click **New transfer**. The wizard lands on **Source** with the five-step rail: **Src → Dest → Map → Validate → Run**.

Under **Where is your data?**, keep **File** selected. Click **Load sample orders CSV** (or upload your own CSV). Wait until the file chip shows **Sample-Orders.csv** with row/column counts and the right panel shows **Detected structure** with typed columns (`INTEGER`, `VARCHAR`, `DECIMAL`, `DATE`).

Click **Continue to Destination →** only after Detected structure is populated — that profile feeds Map and Validate.
Where: Platform → Transfer  ·  or New transfer  →  Load sample orders CSV
Tip: Database and Cloud storage sources work the same way — pick a saved connector, choose table/object, wait for Detected structure, then continue.
Step 2 — Destination: File Export CSV
On **Destination**, choose **Destination Mode**:

**Database / Warehouse** — pick a saved connector (or **Custom connection**) and set schema/table.

**File Export** — used in this example. Select format **CSV** (JSON, Parquet, Excel, and more are available). Optionally set **Output path** to `exports/sample-orders.csv`.

Confirm **Sync defaults** (this example uses **Full append** · Manual approval · Strict validation). Open **Advanced** for overwrite, CDC, SCD2, mirror, cursors, and drift policy.

When the route shows ready, click **Continue to Map**.
Where: Destination Mode → File Export  ·  format CSV  ·  path exports/sample-orders.csv
Tip: Enterprise warehouse path: **Database / Warehouse** → PostgreSQL (or Snowflake / BigQuery) → table such as `public.orders`. The next three steps do not change.
Step 3 — Map: align columns and Accept risk
Map opens **Map columns** with every source field paired to a destination name and type. For `sample-orders.csv` you should see five edges — for example `order_id` → `order_id`, `order_amt` → `order_amount`, with transforms such as **Cast integer**, **Normalize email**, **Cast decimal**, and **Date → ISO**.

Use the filter tabs (**All**, **Review**, **Critical**, **PII**, **Ready**) to focus issues. False-friends stay named: **qty≠amt**, **user≠customer**, **dest collision**. **Approve eligible** will not clear those — Remap dest, or Confirm this pair on the row. When a type cast is lossy (for example DECIMAL → TEXT on a file export), click **Accept risk** on that row.

**Continue to Validate →** stays locked until every blocking map issue is approved or remapped. Then continue.
Where: Map columns → review edges → Accept risk / Approve → Continue to Validate
Tip: Open **Proof** on Map anytime to see confidence and fidelity evidence before Validate.
Step 4 — Validate: clear every blocking gate
Validate runs the full gate set (source readable, destination write access, schema contract, mappings, sample dry-run, data integrity, DDL, capacity, reconcile simulation, plus sync/policy gates).

If a gate blocks — as in this example when `order_amt` (DECIMAL) collapses to TEXT — the dashboard shows **Validation blocked**, which checks failed, and **Suggested fixes** (for example **Remap order_amt → VARCHAR**). Apply the fix, click **Re-run**, and wait until the API decision is **approve**.

**Execute** stays locked while any gate is blocked. That is intentional — do not skip Validate.
Where: Validate dashboard → fix suggested remediations → Re-run until Execute unlocks
Tip: Use **Explain & fix with AI** on Validate for plain-language why/fix, then **Re-run**. See the Preflight gates article for every gate ID.
Step 5 — Run: Execute Transfer and prove in Job Theater
When Validate approves, the **Run** step shows readiness (**Preflight approved**) and unlocks **Execute Transfer**.

If you open Run while Validate is still incomplete, you see **Confirm Validate before write** and Execute stays locked — return to Validate, clear blockers, then come back.

Click **Execute Transfer**. The engine submits the governed job, locks the approved mapping, and opens live telemetry. Then open **Operations → Jobs** (Job Theater): confirm quarantine is empty (or review reasons) and wait for checksum **MATCH** / row fidelity. That MATCH artifact is the archiveable proof of the load.
Where: Run → Execute Transfer  ·  then Operations → Jobs
Tip: After Execute, proof lives on the job — open **Jobs → select the run → Quarantine / Reconcile**. See Job Theater guide for MATCH details.

Write modes (Advanced)
Open **Advanced** on Destination (or Map footer) to set sync mode. Pipelines reuse the same modes on every schedule tick.
**Full append** — keep existing rows; append the full snapshot (default in the example).
**Full overwrite** — replace the target, then load.
**Incremental append** — cursor-based new rows only.
**Incremental deduped** — cursor + primary-key upserts.
**CDC / SCD Type 2 / Mirror** — advanced identity modes (PK required where noted).
**Destination write → Query** — one INSERT/MERGE/UPDATE with `:binds` mapped to source columns. Failed rows quarantine. Not CDC.
**Destination write → Stored procedure** — one CALL/EXEC per row (Informatica connected SQL). SQLite has no dest procedures; dest query INSERT is allowed.

After Run: quarantine & MATCH proof
Rows that fail coerce or policy checks are isolated with **column**, **value**, and **reason** — never silently dropped. After the write, Datawrap reconciles row counts and content hashes. Only then does Job Theater flash **MATCH**.
Tip: Open **Jobs → select the run → Quarantine** before replaying failed rows. Export proof when compliance needs an archive pack.
Job Theater — after Execute, reconcile and row fidelity prove the sample-orders load.

When Validate runs
On Transfer Studio → Validate, and again on every Pipeline tick, Datawrap runs the same gate engine. Execute stays locked until the API decision is approve. Soft or review-grade passes do not unlock write.
Tip: Pipelines cannot skip Validate. A failing gate on a schedule blocks the write the same way as a manual run.

Core gates (before write)
These checks run in Transfer Studio Validate. Open any failing card for the rule text and remediation.
G1 Source readable — source connects and rows can be read
G2 Destination write access — destination is reachable with write/create privilege
G3 Schema contract — source and target schemas are compatible
G4 Column mappings — every column maps above the confidence threshold
G5 Sample dry-run — sample rows pass the same transforms writers use
G9 Data integrity — encoding, required nulls, identity duplicates, precision on the sample
G6 Target DDL — required CREATE / ALTER statements are valid
G7 Staging capacity — destination has headroom for the volume
G8 Sample reconciliation — pre-write sample identity and uniqueness hold (post-load checksum runs after Execute)
Validate — core gate cards (Source readable, Destination write access, Schema contract, …) before any write.

Policy & drift gates
Depending on sync mode and Advanced settings, Validate also enforces sync contract (cursor / primary key), schema change policy, validation posture, and live schema drift against your saved mapping.
Sync contract — cursor and primary key satisfy the chosen sync mode
Schema change policy — detected drift is allowed by policy
Validation posture — overall posture matches Strict / Maximum / Balanced
Schema drift — live schemas still match the saved mapping contract

Procedure: fix a blocked gate
Use this path whenever Validate shows a red or blocking gate.
Open the failing gate card
Click **Run preflight** if gates are still PENDING. Open the failing card and read the rule plus sample evidence. Note whether the issue is mapping, credentials, capacity, encoding, or drift.
Where: Transfer Studio → Validate → gate card
Remediate in Map or Advanced
Approve or rematch columns, **Accept risk** for intentional casts, change sync mode / primary key / cursor, or use **Fix bad data** to strip or quarantine encoding issues — then return to Validate.
Where: Map · Destination → Advanced · Fix bad data
Re-run until Execute unlocks
Execute unlocks only when the API returns **approve**. Then continue to **Run**. If you are unsure, ask Pilot to explain the failing gate in plain language.
Where: Validate → Re-run preflight
Tip: Do not force Execute from the browser alone — governed unlock comes from the control plane.

Semantic roles
Datawrap detects roles like amount, email, identifier, timestamp, and address — not just string name matching.
Map — roles and transforms (Cast, Normalize email, Date → ISO) with confidence and Accept risk.

Synonym dictionary
Accept or reject mapping suggestions. Accepted pairs enter your workspace synonym dictionary for future auto-maps.
Source profiling types feed synonym and role inference before Map opens.

Confidence scores
Each Map edge shows a confidence percentage. Review anything below your threshold — use filter tabs **Review**, **Critical**, **PII**, and **Ready**. Click **Accept risk** for intentional lossy casts, or **Approve** when the edge is clean.

Schema drift detection
Datawrap compares current source and destination schemas against your saved route. Drift warnings appear in Transfer Studio and Datawrap Pilot before the next scheduled run.
New columns in source — review suggested maps
Removed columns — confirm destination still valid
Type changes — preflight type-coercion gate validates casts

What you see on Connectors
The **Connectors** page is the inventory of every saved source and destination in your workspace. Top **health cards** summarize **Connections**, **Healthy**, and **Needs attention**. The table below shows **Last test** and **Last used** so operators know what is safe to schedule in Pipelines.

Use the **Connections** tab for saved credentials. Use **Catalog** only when browsing available driver types — Catalog does not store secrets.
Live workspace — health cards on top, Connections table with Test passed / Test failed.

Procedure: add a connector
Follow this path whenever you onboard a new system. Numbered markers on the screenshots match the live product UI.
Open Connectors
In the signed-in workspace, open **Platform → Connectors**. Confirm the **Connections** tab is selected when you are managing saved credentials (not **Catalog**).

Scan the health cards. If **Needs attention** is greater than zero, open those rows and re-run **Test** before scheduling pipelines against them.
Where: Sidebar → Platform → Connectors
Click New connection — Choose a connector dialog
Click **New connection** (top-right). A modal dialog opens: **Choose a connector**.

Use category chips (**Databases**, **Data Warehouses**, **Files & Formats**, …), search, and status filters (**Certified**, **Source only**, **Test only**, **Planned**). Transfer-ready cards show badges such as **Full Transfer**.

Pick a driver — for example **PostgreSQL**, **MySQL**, **MongoDB**, **Snowflake**, **BigQuery**, **S3**, **CSV / TSV**, or a SQLAlchemy generic. **Planned** catalog entries must not be scheduled in production Pipelines.
Where: Top-right → New connection
Enter credentials and Test
After you pick a driver, the credential form opens (still in the dialog flow). Fill **host**, **database**, and auth (password, key, or cloud credentials). Click **Test** before **Save**. Do not skip Test.

**Test passed** (green) on the Connections table means the driver reached the system — safe to pick in Transfer Studio and Pipelines.

**Test failed** (red) means fix credentials, firewall, or region network access before using the connector. Failed connections block Validate gates later.
Where: Wizard form → Test → Save
Tip: Credentials are encrypted at rest with workspace-scoped keys. Enterprise tenants can enable **BYOK** under **Settings → Enterprise**. Raw passwords never appear in Job Theater logs.
Use it in Transfer Studio
Open **Platform → Transfer**. On **Source** (or later **Destination**), choose **Database** or **Cloud storage**. Your saved healthy connectors appear in the picker.

Continue through **Map → Validate → Run**. A green **Test passed** on Connectors does **not** skip preflight — Validate still runs the full gate set before any production write.
Where: Transfer → Source or Destination → Database

Honest transfer-ready labels
Catalog tiles are not the same as production drivers. Each connector shows one of these readiness states. Only routes with transfer-ready evidence get the production badge — everything else stays labelled honestly.
**Live** — governed transfer path proven; safe for production schedules after Test passed.
**Beta** — works with known limits; review before production Pipelines.
**Planned** — catalog presence only; do not schedule yet.
**Connect-only** — auth works; write path is not transfer-ready.

Native drivers & SQLAlchemy
**PostgreSQL**, **MySQL**, **MongoDB**, **Snowflake**, **BigQuery**, **Redshift**, **S3**, **CSV**, **JSON**, and more ship with upsert and incremental where supported. Generic **SQLAlchemy** URLs extend reach with the same **Validate** preflight path used by native drivers.

What a pipeline is
A **pipeline** is a scheduled Transfer Studio route. Every cadence tick still runs mapping confidence, **Validate** preflight gates, quarantine, and reconciliation proof — recurring does **not** mean less governance.

Create happens on an **inline form** titled **Create recurring sync** (not a side drawer). After you save, clicking a pipeline opens the **right-side detail drawer** with Overview / Schema / History / Config and actions like **Run now**, **Pause**, and **Edit**.
Tip: You need at least two saved connectors (source + destination) under **Platform → Connectors** before **Save pipeline** enables.
Operations → Pipelines — create from empty state or New pipeline in the toolbar.

Procedure: create a pipeline
Follow this exact path in the signed-in workspace. Screenshots are from the live **Create recurring sync** form and pipeline detail drawer — not Jobs.
Open Pipelines
Open **Operations → Pipelines**. The page title is **Pipelines** with the subtitle *Schedule recurring syncs with the same governed transfer engine.*

If none exist yet, the empty state shows **Create pipeline**. The toolbar always offers **Export YAML**, **Import YAML**, **Require signed**, and **New pipeline**.
Where: Sidebar → Operations → Pipelines
Open Create recurring sync
Click **Create pipeline** or **New pipeline**. The page switches to the inline form **Create recurring sync** (*Schedule source → destination with your saved connectors*). A teal status chip shows **Creating your first pipeline** (or **Creating pipeline**).

Fill:

1. **Pipeline name** (example: `Nightly orders sync`)
2. **Source connector** + **Source table|collection**
3. **Destination connector** + **Destination table|collection**

Prefer connectors you already **Test passed** on Connectors, and a route you have proven once in Transfer Studio.
Where: Create pipeline  ·  or New pipeline
Tip: If Source/Destination show **No connectors available**, stop and add connectors under **Platform → Connectors** first — Save stays locked until both sides are selected.
Set Cadence (Preset or Cron)
In the **Cadence** panel, choose **Preset** or **Cron**.

**Preset** tiles: **Hourly**, **Daily**, **Weekly**. Presets are rolling intervals from the last run (or create) — Daily means ~24 hours later, not a fixed wall-clock time.

**Cron** uses a 5-field expression plus **Timezone** (example: `10 10 * * *` daily at 10:10). Next run is computed after save.
Where: Cadence → Preset | Cron
Choose Sync mode + validation policy
In **Sync mode**, pick how rows move. Live tiles include **Full overwrite**, **Full append**, **Incremental append**, **Incremental deduped**, **CDC**, **SCD Type 2**, and **Mirror** (availability depends on connector pair).

For incremental / CDC / SCD2 / Mirror, fill **Cursor column** and/or **Primary key** when shown.

Set **Validation mode** (**Strict** / **Maximum** / **Balanced**), **Schema change policy**, and optionally **Backfill new fields on schema change**.
Where: Sync mode · Validation mode · Schema change policy
Bind Data contract + retries (optional)
In **Data contract**, optionally bind a **SIGNED** contract and enable **Require signed contract before each run (fail-closed)** so unattended ticks cannot write against an unsigned schema.

In **Retry & notifications**, set **Max retries**, **Retry backoff (seconds)**, and toggles **Notify on failure** / **Notify on success**.
Where: Data contract · Retry & notifications
Save pipeline
Scroll to the form footer. Click **Save pipeline** (edit mode shows **Save changes**). On success you get a toast **Pipeline created** and return to the pipeline list/cards.

**Cancel** discards the draft without saving.
Where: Footer → Save pipeline
Open the detail drawer — Run now & History
Click the saved pipeline card/row. The **right-side detail drawer** opens with tabs **Overview**, **Schema**, **History**, and **Config**.

Footer actions: **Run now** (immediate governed tick), **Last job**, **Pause** / **Activate**, **Edit** (reopens the inline form), **Export YAML**, **Delete**.

Use **History** to see prior ticks before jumping to Job Theater.
Where: Click pipeline card → right drawer
Tip: **Edit** closes the drawer and returns you to the same **Create recurring sync** form fields for that pipeline.
Prove each tick in Job Theater
Every cadence tick and every **Run now** creates a job with the same phases as Transfer Studio (gates → write → reconcile). Open **Operations → Jobs**, select the run, and confirm quarantine and reconciliation proof.

Do not confuse the Jobs page with Pipelines — Pipelines owns the schedule; Jobs owns the proof for each tick.
Where: Run now / schedule tick → Operations → Jobs
Tip: Wire **Notify on failure** (or webhooks) before promoting a pipeline to production cadence.

Sync modes (exact product labels)
Pipelines reuse Transfer Studio sync modes. Pick the tile that matches your identity strategy:
**Full overwrite** — replace the target, then load the snapshot
**Full append** — keep existing rows; append the full snapshot
**Incremental append** — cursor/watermark new rows only
**Incremental deduped** — cursor + primary-key upserts
**CDC** — log-based changes (when the source supports it)
**SCD Type 2** — versioned history (primary key required)
**Mirror** — soft-delete dest keys missing from source (`_deleted`; physical COUNT(*) stays; primary key required)
Tip: Failed cells quarantine without silently dropping the rest of the batch — same engine as ad-hoc Transfer Studio runs.

GitOps YAML (optional)
From the Pipelines toolbar you can **Export YAML** / **Import YAML** and optionally **Require signed** contracts for fail-closed unattended runs. Treat exported YAML as the reviewable definition of cadence + route + sync mode for change management.

Redis destination keys
Redis stores each row under `prefix:identity`. Datawrap prefers `id` / `*_id` / `uuid`, then natural keys (`code`, `iso`, `name`, `sku`). Non-unique attributes like `capital` or `city` are never chosen when a stronger key exists. Set **Primary key** on the pipeline Sync mode panel (or on Map for ad-hoc runs) when you need an explicit column.

What a contract is
A **data contract** is a signed schema agreement for a route. Contracts live under **Platform → Contracts**. Pipelines can require a **SIGNED** contract before each tick (**Require signed contract before each run**).
Platform → Contracts — inventory of draft and signed schema agreements.

chunks.section_title: Procedure: bind a contract to a pipeline
chunks.text:
Procedure: bind a contract to a pipeline
Use contracts when unattended Pipelines must fail closed if the schema drifts or is unsigned.
Create or open a contract
Open **Contracts**. Create from a proven Transfer Studio Validate result when available, or open an existing contract card/row. Review schema fields and status (**Draft** vs **Signed**).
Where: Platform → Contracts
Inspect contract detail
Click a contract card/row to open its **detail drawer** (right side). Confirm field types, version, and signature state (**Draft** vs **Signed**). Sign when Owners are ready for production schedules.
Where: Contract card → detail drawer
Bind on Create recurring sync
On **Operations → Pipelines → New pipeline**, open the **Data contract** panel. Select the **SIGNED** contract and enable **Require signed contract before each run (fail-closed)** when unattended ticks must not write without agreement.
Where: Pipelines → Data contract panel
Tip: Unsigned or missing contracts with require-signed enabled block the tick the same way a failed Validate gate does.

Where Transforms live
Open **Operations → Transforms**. This page inventories reusable transform definitions operators can apply on **Map** (cast, normalize email, date → ISO, and custom transforms your tenant enables).
Operations → Transforms — reusable transform inventory for Map and pipelines.

How Transforms relate to Map
During Transfer Studio **Map**, each edge can show a transform (for example **Cast integer**, **Normalize email**). Accepting risk or approving the edge locks that transform into the governed route Pipelines reuse on every tick.
Tip: Changing a production transform usually means editing the route on Map (or the pipeline Config), then re-running Validate before the next schedule tick.
Map — per-column Transform column is where operators see and approve casts.

When to use Pilot
Open **Operations → Pilot**. Ask about failed preflight gates, job status, connector readiness, or mapping suggestions. Pilot uses the same workspace context as Transfer Studio — it does not bypass Validate.
Pilot — natural-language triage on the same governed engine.

Hand off to Transfer Studio
When you need the full wizard, open **Transfer** from Pilot suggestions — maps and gates carry into Source → Destination → Map → Validate → Run.

Example prompts
Pilot understands workspace context — ask about specific jobs, connectors, or mapping decisions.
Why did preflight gate Data integrity fail on my last transfer?
Which connectors are transfer-ready for Snowflake upsert?
Why did order_amt map to total_amount instead of payment_amount?
Show quarantined rows from last night's pipeline

Open the MCP page
Open **System → MCP**. The page shows MCP server status, integration snippets for **Cursor**, **Claude Desktop**, **VS Code**, and custom GPT actions, plus recent tool call logs. Agents inherit workspace RBAC — no raw destination passwords.
System → MCP — status, client snippets, and tool logs for governed agent runs.

Agent security
MCP tools inherit workspace RBAC. Agents cannot read raw connector secrets — only trigger governed operations your role allows. Pipeline ticks and agent runs still must pass Validate before write.

Open Query Playground
Open **Operations → Query**. Pick a saved connector, choose dialect (PostgreSQL, MySQL, Snowflake, BigQuery, or generic SQL), and run read-oriented checks before you map or schedule.
Query — connector picker, SQL editor, and results before Transfer Studio.

Tips
Use Query Playground to validate source data shape before mapping. Format JSON results, clear the editor, and use snippet chips for common patterns. Playground is **read-only** — it refuses CALL/EXEC and DML. Governed writes still go through Transfer Studio / Pipelines.

Bridge to Transfer Studio
When the shape looks right, open **Transfer** and reuse the same connector. On **Source**, choose **Query** (read-only SELECT) or **Stored procedure** (one CALL/EXEC, spooled once). On **Destination**, choose **Query** (one INSERT/MERGE/UPDATE with binds) or **Stored procedure** (one CALL per row). Failed dest statements quarantine — they never silently drop. CDC / SCD2 / mirror refuse callable dest writes. Validated playground queries do not skip Validate.

Open Job Theater
Go to Operations → Jobs (also linked as Theater). Filter All / Running / Completed / Failed. Select a job to open Detail, Mapping, Quarantine, and Log tabs. Theater auto-opens Quarantine when a run completed with rejected rows.
Jobs — select a run to inspect phases, quarantine, and checksum proof.

Job phases
Every ad-hoc transfer and every pipeline tick uses the same phase rail:
Queued — accepted by the control plane
Read — source extract / profile
Gates — Validate decisions applied before write
Write — clean rows land; bad cells quarantine
Reconcile — row counts and content hashes compared
Done — Match, Mismatch, failed, cancelled, or completed with quarantine

Procedure: inspect quarantine
Quarantine means bad values were isolated with column, value, and reason — never silently dropped.
Open the job
Look for Quarantine status or a non-zero rejected count in the stats strip.
Where: Operations → Jobs → select run
Open the Quarantine tab
Review each bad cell: column, offending value, rule, and timestamp. Export for offline review if needed.
Where: Job detail → Quarantine
Fix and re-run
Return to Map or Validate to fix mappings / encoding, then Retry or Resume from checkpoint. Pipeline ticks will fail the same way until the underlying route is fixed.
Where: Open Studio · Retry · Resume from checkpoint
Tip: Completed with quarantine still wrote clean rows — proof may Match on the clean set while quarantine holds the rest.

Checksum MATCH
Gate-8 / post-load proof compares source and destination row counts and content hashes. Theater shows Match or Mismatch with row fidelity. Finance and compliance can treat Match as the archiveable proof of the load — export from the job when required.

Where enterprise settings live
Signed-in Owners open **System → Settings**. Tabs typically include General, Security, Enterprise, SSO, Team, Notifications, AI Models, API Keys, and Audit Logs. Day-to-day operators usually stay on Connectors, Transfer, Pipelines, and Jobs.
System → Settings — Owners configure SSO, Team, Enterprise, and API keys here.

Procedure: configure SSO
Use SAML 2.0 (Okta / Azure AD / OneLogin) or OIDC (Google / Auth0 / Azure AD).
Open Settings → SSO
Choose SAML or OIDC. Paste IdP metadata URL or upload metadata XML. Map roles if your IdP sends group claims.
Where: System → Settings → SSO
Test, then Save
Run Test login with a pilot user. On success you see SSO ready. Save to enforce SSO for the tenant.
Where: SSO → Test · Save
Tip: Keep a break-glass Owner account path documented with IT before enforcing SSO-only.

Team roles
Open **Settings → Team** to invite members by email and assign roles.
Viewer — inspect Jobs, proof, and connectors (no execute)
Editor — create connectors, run Transfer Studio and Pipelines
Owner — SSO, BYOK, Enterprise tab, API keys, Team admin
Team — invite members and assign Viewer / Editor / Owner.

BYOK, region, and audit
Settings → Enterprise sets tenant name, custom domain, data region, MFA, session timeout, and IP allowlist. Optional BYOK wraps connector secrets with your KMS key. Settings → Audit Logs lists mapping decisions, job runs, quarantine events, and MCP calls for SOC 2 / GDPR / HIPAA review. Settings → Security downloads the Security posture report for procurement.

Authentication
Bearer tokens scoped to workspace. Enterprise uses SSO-backed service accounts.
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.datawrap.io/api/v1/connectors

Core endpoints
Catalog, preflight, run, and job status endpoints mirror Transfer Studio behavior.
Canonical prefix is /api/v1 — see docs/API_VERSIONING.md for deprecation policy
GET /api/v1/connectors — list with transfer-ready status
POST /api/v1/preflight — run nine core gates
POST /api/v1/transfer/run — execute governed load
GET /api/v1/connectors/jobs/{id} — status, quarantine, reconciliation
API runs surface in Job Theater with the same stage timeline and checksum proof.

Webhooks
Subscribe to job.completed, job.failed, and pipeline.quarantine_threshold events. Payloads include job ID, gate results, and reconciliation summary — no row payloads unless explicitly configured.
POST /api/v1/webhooks
{ "url": "https://your.app/hooks/dataflow", "events": ["job.completed"] }

What is quarantine?
Rows that fail validation during load are isolated with the column, value, and reason — never silently dropped. Open Operations → Jobs → Quarantine on the run to inspect or export them.
Quarantine and proof live on the job — open Theater to inspect failed rows.

Who can run transfers?
Editors and Owners can create connectors and execute Transfer Studio / Pipelines. Viewers can open Jobs and review MATCH / quarantine proof. Roles are assigned under Settings → Team (and can come from IdP group claims when SSO is configured).

Do pipelines skip preflight?
No. Every schedule tick reuses the same Validate gates and post-load checksum path as a manual transfer. A failing gate blocks the write; the tick appears Failed in Jobs until the route is fixed.

chunks.section_title: How is data protected in transit and at rest?
chunks.text:
How is data protected in transit and at rest?
Connectors use TLS to sources and destinations. Secrets are encrypted at rest (optional customer BYOK). Quarantine replaces silent drops; post-load checksums prove what landed. Download the Security posture report from Settings → Security for procurement questionnaires.

chunks.section_title: How is Datawrap different from ETL scripts?
chunks.text:
How is Datawrap different from ETL scripts?
Semantic mapping with confidence, fail-fast Validate gates, quarantine instead of silent coerce, and checksum MATCH after write — with SSO, RBAC, and audit built for enterprise teams.
